text: {"lessons":["Selling Stock A for a small gain, then buying it back and selling at a loss, reminds me not to let the satisfaction of realizing gains drive repeated trades; I need a consistent, forward-looking plan.","I sold several positions at steep losses, but waiting too long to reassess them did not prevent losses from growing. I should use clear, stock-specific risk limits rather than anchor on my average cost.","My account kept declining even when I made no trades, so I should review total exposure and diversification regularly and not mistake inactivity—or trading one position at a time—for portfolio risk management."]}
